text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 2.3% today as oil prices climbed to a 6-week high following escalating tensions between Iran and the U.S. in the Middle East. Crude jumped above $99 a barrel after reports of Iranian attacks on U.S. Navy ships, and refineries across the country are running at 98% capacity — near maximum utilization. For a refiner like Marathon, higher oil prices combined with full-throttle operations mean stronger profit margins on the fuel they produce and sell.

The stock has gained nearly 10% over the past two weeks as these geopolitical risks have built up and energy markets have tightened. With oil storage levels relatively modest and demand steady, the refining sector benefits when crude gets more expensive and production constraints limit supply.
